The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook. However, consistent with the credit-channel literature (e.g., Bernanke–Gertler; Oliner and Rudebusch; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist), the Fed’s rapid move to the zero lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount window support, and dollar swap lines should lower external finance premia and dampen amplification through firms and households. With market-based inflation compensation down but survey-based long-run expectations little changed, the response also aligns with inflation-forecast-targeting guidance (Svensson) to keep expectations anchored near 2 percent while deploying balance-sheet tools appropriate for a potential liquidity trap. Overall tone remains cautious-negative but partially mitigated by policy support.
